items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: All clarinet players emulated, uh, or tried to, Benny Goodman.

ctx.x: Amazing. Can you remember that before, like in, uh, before the war, can you remember it at all? I mean, there was... Before the war. Or, say, around early, very early 40s, there really wasn't any, any jazz.

No, there was, there was jazz in a sense, but it was, uh, uh, currently the modern jazz. There wasn't any, uh, Dixieland. We played, uh, whatever was, uh, in the vein, all clarinet players emulated, uh, or tried to, Benny Goodman. All the saxophone players were trying to play like Vito Musso. And all the trumpet players were another Harry James. And, uh, the boys that did manage to keep this Dixieland music alive throughout all of these years, they weren't working too often, too regularly. They'd play a funeral,…
What were the, what was the, what was it that made you change your policy here, say in the 50s or whenever it was, away from, um, a music orientation to more of, uh, entertainment?
